track.why: Aug 11 2023 summit; starts and ends within 50 m of the Staircase pin, leaves trail just below First Divide, summit 7 m from our pin. Our catalog has exactly one route from Staircase and the track follows its described line. Flagged one-way by the mechanical check (not complete); the report calls it a single-day round trip of about 29 miles.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Jul 8 2023, Staircase start and summit within 4 m, but distance 50.6 mi looks doubled and no report; second choice.

facts.text: In August, the full day from Staircase to the summit and back is roughly 29 miles with around 7,000 ft of gain, so it is a very long single push or an overnight at the lower camps.
After First Divide the way drops about 500 ft to a meadow basin; cross it and work up through brush, then talus and scree, then a steep heather slope below the summit blocks.
Coming down in August, keeping well to the climber's left through the lower brush helped avoid the second steep, cliffy bushwhack.
The upper heather slope is steep; a slip there could mean a long tumble, and it is far worse if wet.
The south summit block is exposed with crumbly rock and felt closer to Class 4 than the rest of the route.
Trekking poles or microspikes for the steep upper heather slope (late summer, dry)
